title: Conditions for Selling a Kessler GAP Waiver Addendum
content:
# Conditions for Selling a Kessler GAP Waiver Addendum

A Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda waiver is sold only on a purchase deal financed by a dealer-arranged installment contract. A cash deal, an outside-lender deal, a fleet net-terms deal and a lease cannot carry one; no waiver may be attached to a lease.

## Conditions on the vehicle

- The vehicle's condition must be one of the conditions the waiver accepts.
- Its age at sale, counted as the sale year less the model year, may not exceed the waiver's greatest vehicle age.
- A vehicle in commercial use is covered only where the waiver covers commercial use.

## Conditions on the contract and the price

- The contract term must lie between the waiver's shortest and longest contract term, and where the waiver term must equal the contract term, it does.
- The amount financed must lie between the waiver's smallest and largest amount financed.
- The waiver's price may not exceed its highest price.

The figures for each condition are those of the waiver's eligibility schedule.

## The vehicle value basis

The vehicle value basis is the vehicle's MSRP for a new vehicle and its NADA retail value at sale for a used or certified vehicle, limited to the source the waiver's value source names (MSRP, NADA retail value, or MSRP or NADA retail value by condition).

## Qualifying examples (hypothetical deals)

| Deal | Result |
|---|---|
| New vehicle, dealer-arranged installment contract, terms within the waiver's limits | may carry the waiver |
| Same vehicle bought with an outside lender's loan | may not carry a waiver |
| Vehicle leased | may not carry a waiver |
| Model year Year 3, sold in Year 9 (6 years old), waiver with a 7-year limit | age condition met |
| Model year Year 1, sold in Year 9 (8 years old), waiver with a 7-year limit | age condition not met |
| Used vehicle, waiver whose value source is MSRP or NADA retail value by condition | value basis is the NADA retail value at sale |
